description: Key milestones in the history of medicine and healthcare

hippocrates.four_humors: Blood, phlegm, yellow bile, black bile; imbalance causes disease

ancient_medicine.ancient_egypt: Edwin Smith Papyrus (c. 1600 BCE); surgical procedures; evidence-based treatments
ancient_medicine.ayurveda: Indian system; 5,000+ years old; mind-body-spirit approach; herbal medicine
ancient_medicine.galen: Greek physician (130–210 CE); extensive anatomy (from animals); dominant in Europe for 1,400 years

major_milestones.1543: Vesalius publishes De Humani Corporis Fabrica; corrects Galen's errors with human dissection
major_milestones.1628: William Harvey describes blood circulation; heart as pump
major_milestones.1846: First use of ether for surgical anesthesia (Morton, Massachusetts General Hospital)
major_milestones.1847: Ignaz Semmelweis discovers hand-washing prevents infection; rejected by peers
major_milestones.1854: John Snow traces cholera outbreak to water pump; birth of epidemiology
major_milestones.1860s: Louis Pasteur develops germ theory; pasteurization
major_milestones.1898: Marie and Pierre Curie discover radium; radiation therapy begins
major_milestones.1901: Karl Landsteiner discovers ABO blood groups; enables safe transfusions
major_milestones.1921: Frederick Banting and Charles Best isolate insulin; transforms diabetes treatment
major_milestones.1953: Watson, Crick, Franklin, Wilkins determine DNA double helix structure
major_milestones.1967: First successful heart transplant (Christiaan Barnard, Cape Town)
major_milestones.1978: First IVF baby born (Louise Brown, UK)
major_milestones.1983: HIV virus identified; AIDS epidemic defined
major_milestones.1998: First targeted cancer therapy (imatinib for CML)
major_milestones.2006: HPV vaccine approved; first vaccine to prevent cancer
major_milestones.2020: COVID-19 pandemic; mRNA vaccines developed in under a year

epidemics_pandemics.bubonic_plague: 1347–1351; Black Death killed 30–60% of European population; ~75 million deaths
epidemics_pandemics.1918_flu: Spanish Flu; 50–100 million deaths; worst pandemic in recorded history
epidemics_pandemics.smallpox: Killed 300 million in 20th century; eradicated 1980 by global vaccination
epidemics_pandemics.polio: Epidemic peaked 1950s; Salk (1955) and Sabin (1961) vaccines; nearly eradicated
epidemics_pandemics.hiv_aids: ~38 million living with HIV; 40 million deaths since 1981; antiretroviral therapy transforms prognosis
epidemics_pandemics.covid_19: 2019–present; SARS-CoV-2; ~7 million confirmed deaths; accelerated mRNA vaccine technology

evidence_based_medicine.definition: Integrating clinical expertise with best available research evidence and patient values
evidence_based_medicine.rct: Randomized Controlled Trial; gold standard for testing interventions
evidence_based_medicine.peer_review: Scientific quality control; reviewed by independent experts before publication
